validity.recommendation: Existence, classification, length, capacity, cost and start-year are all well supported — keep the row. But drop/replace the current Diameter [ref] (sgc-oc.com PDF): it is a non-technical environmental summary for the unrelated Baysun GPZ / Surhan Gas Chemical field-development project (a 2017-founded PSA operator), and does not mention 'Shurtan-Sherabad', 'Shurtan', 'Sherabad' or '800' anywhere in its ~2,000-line text (confirmed by full-text extraction). Diameter=800mm could not be independently confirmed from any other source either — leave it flagged uncited rather than treat it as verified.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strong, independent, multi-decade confirmation. (1) mineral.ru, 2003-09-04, republishing an Interfax wire quoting an Uzbekneftegaz source: pipeline completed, 193 km, ~1 bcm/y capacity, cost ~90bn sum (~$92.4M), financed by Uzbekneftegaz, to be operated by Uztransgaz, built specifically to let southern Uzbekistan (Surkhandarya + south Kashkadarya) stop routing gas through Turkmenistan via the Kelif-Dushanbe/Kelif-Mubarek pipelines. (2) cabar.asia, 2016-03-11, an independent later analysis piece on Uzbekistan's oil & gas sector (different author/outlet/date, not the same wire): repeats 193 km / ~1 bcm/y / built 2003 / same bypass-Turkmenistan rationale, and adds it supplies gas to Tajikistan on a compensation basis via Leninabad-region transit. (3) gazeta.uz, 2021-04-06 (on a $900M VEB.RF/Gazprombank Surkhandarya gas-field financing story): independently describes the 'existing/operating (действующий) trunk gas pipeline Shurtan-Sherabad' as running 10 km from the planned Baysun GPZ site — confirms it as a real, named, still-active piece of infrastructure 18 years after construction. oilcapital.ru (2003-09-03) also carries the story but traces to the same Interfax wire as mineral.ru, so it does NOT count as a second independent source on its own — cabar.asia and gazeta.uz are the genuinely independent corroborators. CLASSIFICATION: correct. All three sources call it a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/main gas pipeline) supplying whole regions, not a gathering/feeder line — transmission is right. DUPLICATE: checked against the 18-row roster. No overlap — the whole point of this line (per mineral.ru) was to give the south an ALTERNATIVE to the existing Kelif-Dushanbe (P6937) / Kelif-Mubarek (P6965/P6966) routes, which cross Turkmen territory; Shurtan-Sherabad deliberately runs through Uzbek territory only. Different corridor, not a relabel or segment double-count of any roster row. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Uzbekneftegaz 100% is directly supported by mineral.ru ('финансировалось за счет средств компании "Узбекнефтегаза"'); note Uztransgaz is named as the OPERATOR, a distinct fact from ownership — not a conflict since GEM's Owner column tracks ownership, and Operator is not tracked on this tab. SPEC: length (193 km) and capacity (1 bcm/y — explicitly 'около 1 млрд кубометров в год') both agree exactly with GEM across mineral.ru + cabar.asia — this REFUTES the hypothesis that Capacity=1.00 is a units/typo defect; 1 bcm/y for a regional feeder-scale trunk is exactly what both independent sources report. SegmentCost ($92.4M / 90bn sum) matches GEM's 92,400,000 USD exactly, sourced to mineral.ru (single source, medium tier). Diameter=800mm is the one spec value with NO independent confirmation found anywhere (checked Russian- and English-language searches, Uztransgaz-adjacent material, technical literature) — and the sheet's own citation for it is simply the wrong document (verified: full PDF text-extracted, zero occurrence of 'Шуртан', 'Шерабад', or '800'; it's SGC-OC's environmental non-technical summary for the Baysun gas processing plant/Surhan gas field project). Recommend a fresh researcher pass specifically hunting Uztransgaz technical/asset-register material for the true diameter, and pulling the bad citation in the meantime.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: No evidence of decommissioning, replacement, or status change found. Best direct confirmation of continued operation is gazeta.uz, 2021-04-06, which independently describes it as the 'действующий магистральный газопровод «Шуртан-Шерабад»' (the operating trunk pipeline). Searched specifically for evidence newer than the sheet's 2024-09-10 LastUpdated (repair/reconstruction news, Uztransgaz 2024 annual/ESG report, winter 2024-25 and 2025-26 gas-crisis coverage for Surkhandarya) and found none naming this pipeline by name post-2021 — the closest is a 2025-10-17 gazeta.uz piece on a Kumkurgan-district (Surkhandarya) gas shortage, but its stated cause is delayed LPG-cylinder deliveries from Lukoil plus a nationwide ~6.6% YoY production decline, i.e. an upstream supply/production problem, not a report that the transmission pipeline itself is down or decommissioned — so it is not cited as pipeline-specific evidence, only noted here as context that the southern gas-supply system this line is part of remains actively in use and under public discussion as of Oct 2025. Nothing found contradicts 'operating'; recorded status stands.

fills.researcher_notes: Both sources describe the pipeline as completed/operating; gazeta.uz 2021 independently calls it 'действующий' (operating) — see Status [ref] duplicated logic under status_reviews.
A natural-gas trunk pipeline throughout all sources ('газопровод' / natural gas pipeline); trivially confirmed.
Both call it a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/main pipeline) supplying whole regions — transmission, not gathering/feeder.
mineral.ru is dated 2003-09-04 reporting completion; cabar.asia (2016, independent analysis) separately states it was built in 2003.

Both sources independently give 'около 1 млрд кубометров в год' (~1 bcm/year) — exactly matches GEM's 1.00 bcm/y. This REFUTES the hypothesized units/typo defect (task hypothesis #2): 1 bcm/y is the correct, sourced figure for this regional feeder-scale trunk, not an error.
Both sources independently give 'протяжённость ... составляет 193 км' (length is 193 km) — exact match.

Inferential but well-grounded: the pipeline's route starts at Shurtan per mineral.ru/cabar.asia/gazeta.uz, and neftegaz.ru's technical entry confirms Shurtan is an active gas-condensate field in Kashkadarya region (discovered 1956, industrial production since 1980) — the natural source point for a pipeline named for it. No source explicitly states 'gas sourced from the Shurtan field feeds this line', so treat as medium-tier, not high.

StartLocation/EndLocation/CountryOrArea confirm the existing sheet values (Shurtan→Sherabad, both Uzbekistan) across all three sources. Adds previously-blank province fields: Shurtan sits in Kashkadarya (Qashqadaryo) region (neftegaz.ru technical entry: field in Guzar district, Kashkadarya region); Sherabad is the seat of Sherabad (Sherobod) district, Surkhandarya (Surxondaryo) region (administrative geography, uncontested). Province fills are single/tertiary-sourced (medium tier) — basic uncontested administrative geography, not a disputed research finding. | POLICY (source_roster.md: Wikipedia is never cited directly; studfile.net is a tertiary re-upload host, same class as the blocklisted wikidot). The ru.wikipedia Sherabad-district page was dropped from this cell; the Sherabad/Surkhandarya admin placement should be re-cited from an official gazetteer (GeoNames or the Uzbek State Committee on Statistics) if it is to be asserted. The two retained refs (mineral.ru, neftegaz.ru) independently carry the endpoints and the Kashkadarya placement, so the cell remains sourced.

mineral.ru (Interfax-sourced, quoting an Uzbekneftegaz spokesperson) gives cost 'about 90 billion sum (≈$92.4 million)' — exact match to GEM's 92,400,000 USD. Single independent source found for this figure (cabar.asia does not repeat it), so medium tier.

summary: P2698 Shurtan-Sherabad: existence/classification/duplicate all confirmed clean by 3 independent sources across 2003-2021 (bypasses Turkmenistan, distinct corridor from Kelif-Mubarek/Kelif-Dushanbe); length 193km and capacity 1.00 bcm/y both independently verified exact (refutes the units-defect hypothesis), cost $92.4M matches; one concern flagged — the existing Diameter [ref] (sgc-oc.com PDF) is a wrong/unrelated document (about a different, unrelated gas-field project) and 800mm remains uncited after independent search.
